items.title: Section: Truth's Outer Limit — Why the Bodhisattva's Purified Truth Admits No Further Refinement

items.zh: 如是境界為最第一、真如無上、所知邊際，齊此一切正法思擇皆悉退還，不能越度。
items.en: This object is the very foremost; it is suchness unsurpassed, the outer limit of the knowable. Up to this point — and no further — does all reflection on the true teaching turn back; it cannot pass beyond.

items.title: Section: Neither "Existence" Nor "Non-Existence" — The Two Extremes True Reality Must Reject

items.zh: 又安立此真實義相，當知即是無二所顯。
items.en: Moreover, when this mark of true reality is established in words, it should be understood as precisely what is revealed by the non-dual — by neither of two extremes.
The "two" spoken of here are: existence, and non-existence.

items.title: "Existence" Analysed — The Imputed Nature That Is the Root of All Conceptual Proliferation

items.zh: 此中有者，謂所安立假說自性，
items.en: Here, "existence" refers to the imputed nature that has been established in language.

items.zh: 即是世間長時所執，亦是世間一切分別戲論根本。
items.en: This is precisely what the world has clung to since beginningless time, and it is the very root of all the world's discriminative conceptual proliferation.

items.zh: 或謂為色、受、想、行、識，或謂眼、耳、鼻、舌、身、意，或復謂為地、水、火、風，或謂色、聲、香、味、觸、法，或謂為善、不善、無記、或謂生滅、或謂緣生，或謂過去、未來、現在，或謂有為，或謂無為，或謂此世，或謂他世，或謂日月，或復謂為所見、所聞、所覺、所知、所求、所得，意隨尋伺，最後乃至或謂涅槃。如是等類，是諸世間共了諸法假說自性，是名為有。

items.title: "Non-Existence" Analysed — The Opposite Extreme of Denying Even Dependent Origination Itself

items.zh: 言非有者，謂即諸色假說自性，乃至涅槃假說自性，無事無相，假說所依，一切都無。
items.en: "Non-existence" means this: with respect to the imputed nature of form, and so on up to the imputed nature of nirvāṇa, it is asserted that there is no substance and no characteristic whatsoever — that even what the imputation depends on does not exist at all.

items.zh: 假立言說依彼轉者皆無所有，是名非有。
items.en: That on the basis of which imputed language actually operates is said to be utterly nonexistent — this is called "non-existence."

items.title: Section: "Neither" — The Middle Way That Resolves Both Extremes at Once

items.zh: 先所說有，今說非有，有及非有二俱遠離，法相所攝真實性事，是名無二。
items.en: What was earlier called "existence," and what is now called "non-existence" — abandoning both existence and non-existence together, the true reality that belongs to the nature of phenomena is called the non-dual.

items.zh: 由無二故，說名中道，遠離二邊，亦名無上。
items.en: Because it is non-dual, it is called the middle way; because it departs from both extremes, it is also called unsurpassed.

items.title: Buddha and Bodhisattva's Differing Degree of Purity in This Same Wisdom

items.zh: 佛世尊智於此真實已善清淨，諸菩薩智於此真實學道所顯。
items.en: The wisdom of the buddhas, the world-honoured ones, has become thoroughly purified with respect to this truth. The wisdom of bodhisattvas, with respect to this same truth, is what is revealed by wisdom still in training.

items.zh: 又即此慧，是諸菩薩能得無上正等菩提廣大方便。何以故？

items.title: Section: Correct View of Birth-and-Death — Neither the Ordinary Being's Craving Nor the Hearer's Aversion

items.zh: 以諸菩薩處於生死，彼彼生中修空勝解，善能成熟一切佛法及諸有情。又能如實了知生死，不於生死以無常等行深心厭離。
items.en: Because bodhisattvas dwell within birth-and-death, in each and every life they cultivate resolute conviction in emptiness, thereby becoming able to bring both the buddha-dharma and sentient beings to full maturity. They are also able to truly understand birth-and-death as it actually is, without developing, through contemplating impermanence and the like, a deep-seated aversion towards birth-and-death itself.

items.zh: 若諸菩薩不能如實了知生死，則不能於貪瞋癡等一切煩惱深心棄捨；不能棄捨諸煩惱故，便雜染心受諸生死；由雜染心受生死故，不能成熟一切佛法及諸有情。若諸菩薩於其生死以無常等行深心厭離，是則速疾入般涅槃；彼若速疾入般涅槃，尚不能成熟一切佛法及諸有情，況能證無上正等菩提。
items.en: If bodhisattvas cannot truly understand birth-and-death, they cannot deeply abandon greed, hatred, delusion, and all other afflictions; unable to abandon these afflictions, they undergo birth-and-death with a defiled mind; and undergoing birth-and-death with a defiled mind in this way, they cannot bring the buddha-dharma or sentient beings to maturity. But if bodhisattvas develop, through contemplating impermanence and the like, a deep-seated aversion towards birth-and-death, they will swiftly enter final nirvāṇa — and having swiftly entered final nirvāṇa, they will be unable even to bring the buddha-dharma and sentient beings to maturity, let alone realise unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

items.title: Section: Correct View of Nirvāṇa — Neither Feared Nor Overly Craved, the Great Expedient Towards Buddhahood

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，由習如是空勝解故，則於涅槃不深怖畏，亦於涅槃不多願樂。若諸菩薩深怖涅槃，即便於彼涅槃資糧不能圓滿。由於涅槃深怖畏故，不見涅槃勝利功德；由不見故，便於涅槃遠離一切清淨勝解。若諸菩薩於其涅槃多住願樂，是則速疾入般涅槃；彼若速疾入般涅槃，則便不能成熟佛法及諸有情。
items.en: Moreover, because bodhisattvas have cultivated this resolute conviction in emptiness, they neither deeply dread nirvāṇa nor excessively long for it. If bodhisattvas deeply dread nirvāṇa, they will be unable to bring the requisites for realising it to fulfilment ... and if bodhisattvas dwell excessively in longing for nirvāṇa, they will swiftly enter final nirvāṇa — and having swiftly entered final nirvāṇa, they will be unable to bring the buddha-dharma and sentient beings to maturity.

items.zh: 當知此中，若不如實了知生死，即雜染心流轉生死；若於生死深心厭離，即便速疾入般涅槃。若於涅槃深心怖畏，即於能證涅槃資糧不能圓滿；若於涅槃多住願樂，即便速疾入般涅槃。是諸菩薩，於證無上正等菩提無大方便。若能如實了知生死，即無染心流轉生死。若於生死不以無常等行深心厭離，即不速疾入般涅槃。若於涅槃不深怖畏，即能圓滿涅槃資糧；雖於涅槃見有微妙勝利功德，而不深願速證涅槃。是諸菩薩，於證無上正等菩提有大方便。
是大方便，依止最勝空性勝解；是故菩薩修習學道所攝最勝空性勝解，名為能證如來妙智廣大方便。
items.en: This great expedient means rests on the most supreme resolute conviction in emptiness; therefore a bodhisattva's cultivation, within the scope of the path still in training, of this most supreme conviction in emptiness is called the great expedient means for realising the Tathāgata's wondrous wisdom.

items.title: Entering Phenomena's Selflessness — Free of All Conceptual Discrimination, Yet Never Denying Cause and Effect

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，由能深入法無我智，於一切法離言自性如實知已，達無少法及少品類可起分別。
items.en: Moreover, bodhisattvas, through their ability to deeply enter the wisdom of phenomena's selflessness, truly understand every phenomenon's inexpressible nature — and having understood it, they realise that not even the slightest phenomenon, nor the slightest category of phenomena, remains capable of giving rise to discrimination.

items.zh: 唯取其事，唯取真如。不作是念，此是唯事，是唯真如；但行於義。
items.en: They take only the event, and take only suchness. They do not form the thought "this is merely the event" or "this is merely suchness" — they simply proceed directly in accordance with the meaning.

blocks.text: The central argument of the chapter: reality is "non-dual", free of two extremes. A short passage (0486c27) and one at 0487b04 are untranslated.
"This object is the very foremost: suchness unsurpassed, the outer limit of the knowable. Up to this point, and no further, does all reflection on the true teaching turn back."
Reality, put into words, "is revealed by the non-dual, by neither of two extremes": **existence** and **non-existence**.
"'Existence' refers to the imputed nature established in language: what the world has clung to since beginningless time, the very root of all conceptual proliferation."
"'Non-existence' means asserting, of the imputed nature of form up to nirvāṇa, that there is no substance whatsoever: that even what the imputation depends on does not exist at all."
"Abandoning both existence and non-existence together, the true reality of phenomena is called the non-dual. Because it is non-dual, it is called the middle way."

Through conviction in emptiness, bodhisattvas "truly understand birth and death" without craving it, yet without the deep aversion that would make them flee it; they "neither deeply dread nirvāṇa nor excessively long for it". This balance is "the great expedient means for realising the Tathāgata's awakening".

Entering the selflessness of phenomena, "they take only the event, and take only suchness. They do not form the thought 'this is merely the event' or 'merely suchness'; they simply proceed in accordance with the meaning." Venerable Miào Jìng: the dependent nature is still there.

quiz.q: "Up to this point all reflection turns back and cannot pass beyond." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain?
options: all wisdom reflecting on the Dharma stops here and must turn back
quiz.why: "This object is the very foremost; it is suchness unsurpassed, the outer limit of the knowable. Up to this point — and no further — does all reflection on the true teaching turn back." Venerable Miào Jìng: all the wisdom that reflects on and examines the true Dharma stops here — it must turn back.

quiz.q: The mark of true reality is "revealed by the non-dual." How do the masters explain negation (遮) and affirmation (表)?
options: Cháng Bǎi: affirmation is 表, negation 遮; Miào Jìng: "non-dual" is negation, "dual" affirmation
quiz.why: "When this mark of true reality is established in words, it should be understood as precisely what is revealed by the non-dual." Master Cháng Bǎi: expressing affirmatively is 表; expressing by negation is 遮. Venerable Miào Jìng: "non-dual" is negation; "dual" is affirmation.

quiz.q: Imputed nature is "the root of all the world's conceptual proliferation." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: from these names, many writers have produced much proliferation
quiz.why: "This is precisely what the world has clung to since beginningless time, and it is the very root of all the world's discriminative conceptual proliferation." Master Cháng Bǎi: based on these names, many writers have produced a great deal of proliferation.

quiz.q: "Non-existence" claims "no substance and no characteristic." How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish 事 and 相?
options: 事 concerns substance, 相 outward appearance
quiz.why: "'Non-existence' means this: with respect to the imputed nature of form … up to the imputed nature of nirvāṇa, it is asserted that there is no substance and no characteristic whatsoever." Master Cháng Bǎi: 事 is said of the substance; 相 of the outward appearance.

quiz.q: "The true reality belonging to the nature of phenomena is called the non-dual." Which natures does it include, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the dependent and the perfected natures
quiz.why: "Abandoning both existence and non-existence together, the true reality that belongs to the nature of phenomena is called the non-dual." Master Cháng Bǎi: true reality is of two kinds — included in the dependent and perfected natures.

quiz.q: In each life the bodhisattva "cultivates conviction in emptiness." How does Master Cháng Bǎi describe it?
options: remove worldly perception, establish the supramundane — the perception of phenomena's emptiness
quiz.why: "Because bodhisattvas dwell within birth-and-death, in each and every life they cultivate resolute conviction in emptiness." Master Cháng Bǎi: first remove worldly perception and establish supramundane perception — the perception of phenomena's emptiness is supramundane.

quiz.q: "If bodhisattvas deeply dread nirvāṇa" — what is the ordinary being's fear, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: there's no self in nirvāṇa — how could that be all right?
quiz.why: "If bodhisattvas deeply dread nirvāṇa, they will be unable to bring the requisites for realising it to fulfilment." Venerable Miào Jìng: there's no self in nirvāṇa — how could that be all right?
